Name: Marissa-Anneke Collins
Question: Is it true that good semi-truck drivers float gears? What happens inside the transmission when you do that, and is that bad?
Answer: A good driver will learn their equipment beforehand. Floating gears isn’t difficult, and I wouldn’t consider that as a way of determining if a driver is good or not. If, for example, they jumped into one of the rare Volvos in the US with the 14 speed as it was called and began floating that one, it would be a strike against them because that is a synchromesh transmission. A good driver would learn that before the fact. As far as what happens in the transmission, if done right, nothing out of the ordinary. The gear teeth line up and it goes into gear, else they end up playing ‘grind it til you find it” (which can happen even if you double clutch). On the maintenance side, we prefer that the drivers float rather than double clutch. A number of them learned how to drive in a manual with a regular passenger car, pickup truck, what have you. From that, they got into the habit of pushing the clutch pedal all the way down. Which is normal for a synchromesh transmission. On a unsynchronized transmission (which is typical for trucks in that class of North American manufacture), the transmissions are unsynchronized - the driver does the rev matching to account for the absence of a synchronizer gear. Which is a developed skill of course, but there’s more to driving than just shifting. You might have the smoothest crash box shifting known to man, but if you can’t go down a hill without fading out your brakes, you’re not a good driver. One thing the crash boxes have which a synchromesh transmission doesn’t is a clutch brake. Which is just a friction surface that makes contact when the clutch pedal is fully depressed. It’s for when you’re stopped, so you can get into gear again. If you’re double clutching as you’re going down the road and depressing the clutch pedal all the way, you’re wearing out that clutch brake.

Name: Marissa-Anneke Collins
Question: You have to pick one gun between Colt 1911, Glock 17, Sig Sauer P226, Smith and Wesson M&P, and CZ75. Which one is it?
Answer: Seeing as I own an M&P9, M&P9C, M&P Shield 9, and M&P Shield 45, and that I’m still feeling divided over getting the P365 rather than the M&P Shield Plus, you should be able to tell that I absolutely hate them. Glock 17… the first handgun I bought from an FFL was a Glock 19. Not really thrilled with the sights or the grip angle of these, but I have no doubts about their reliability. It seeing as I already have two comparable pistols I prefer for different purposes - an M&P9 and a Canik Rival - adding a Glock 17 to the mix doesn’t offer me anything new. Sig Sauer P226… I inherited two. Bit on the chunky side for me. The one with the .357 Sig and .40 barrels, I don’t fire that one at all. The 9mm, I take to the range from time to time. Not a huge fan of these. I did buy a P220 in .45 with an eye towards using it in competition. In the end I figured that, even with the tuning I wanted, the 1911 would still be a preferable competition gun. Colt 1911… which specific model? One of the guns I use in competition is a modified Gold Cup (the other being a Les Baer Concept VI). I also inherited a couple others, which aren’t competition grade but they are pleasurable to shoot on account of having really great triggers. Not my choice for carry, though. So I’d probably go with the CZ75, since that’s the one which would be new to me.

Question: Why does the washer fluid on my 2020 Kenworth T680 (both sides) only come out the top half of my windshield, leaving the middle to the bottom still unclean?
Answer: I don’t expect they’d have changed this since the last model year of T680 I worked on, but the nozzles should be mounted to the wiper arms. You might have them too far to the end of the wiper arms.

Name: Marissa-Anneke Collins
Question: I have posted questions to which a left-winger gives a hate-filled, racist answer, and then further comments are disabled. It's obvious why they do this. But how is this done?
Answer: Fair chance they blocked you, and I would’ve done the same already if I encountered your content with any regularity on my feed. It’s not about your politics and where ours may not align, but I read some of your answers and it’s all really lowbrow shit. I’ve blocked right wingers and left wingers and muted left- and right leaning spaces for this exact reason. One of the things I used to like about Quora is that there were people who I may have seen eye-to-eye with on very little or nothing at all, but they could elaborate on their point of view without resorting to ad hominem, and you would understand why they stood where they did and how they arrived there. Granted, they often didn’t receive the same courtesy in return from those on Quora of opposing viewpoints. You, on the other hand, are just shitposting, which makes it especially disappointing as you claim a credential indicating that you’re well educated. That asked, they may have disabled comments on an individual answer, which if you click on the ellipsis on the right hand side at the top of the answer (as the person who posted that answer), the option to disable comments appears there. They may have comments disabled on all of their answers. How to do that… in the app (at least the iOS one), at the upper left corner will be your displayed avatar. Click on that, and a menu appears. One of the options will be “privacy”. Once you click on that and scroll down, you’ll see the “Allow comments” option… there are no other options and you can’t limit the ability to comment on your answers to, say, your followers or anything of the sort. Either you have comments enabled and anyone can comment on them (with exception to people you’ve blocked) or nobody can.

Name: Marissa-Anneke Collins
Question: How many people do you block on Quora per day?
Answer: At least one, usually more. Of course there’s a certain troll (who I’m convinced isn’t actually the works of just one person) who makes multitude of accounts, but I happen across shitposters in my feed, and of course people acting like dickheads in my comments. There’s no rhyme or reason to engage with them, so I just take out the trash and be done with it. I could sit and watch paint dry and it would be more interesting than the ramblings of someone bantering on about what a tough guy he is while remaining oblivious that his ramblings just scream out, “fragility” (and this happened - again - earlier today), or people who just get on Quora and do nothing but try to pick petty little slap fights in the comments. Not inclined to put any effort into dealing with these nobodies, so block, mute, delete that shit. What kills me is that now a lot of these people make comments or posts about, “If you block me, it means I’ve won”. I don’t think they really believe that bullshit, it’s just copium for the tantrum they throw because they’re (purportedly) adults who are asshurt at not being able to argue on the Internet. For real, what exactly do they really think they’ve won? And why do they think anyone else cares that they feel (or pretend to) that way?
